stages.name: Profit maximisation and shareholders
stages.title: Profit maximisation and shareholders
stages.sub: After this the student can explain why maximising profit benefits the shareholders who own the firm.

steps.q: A firm keeps producing extra units as long as each one adds more to revenue than it costs to make. At the output where the next unit would add exactly as much cost as revenue, what has the firm found?
steps.right: The output that gives the biggest possible profit
steps.wrong: The output that gives the biggest possible revenue
steps.hint: Beyond this point, extra units would cost more than they bring in.

steps.q: A firm produces at this output rather than a lower one where costs are easily covered. Compared to just covering its costs, what does producing here leave the firm with?
steps.right: The largest amount of profit left over
steps.wrong: The same profit, just spread differently
steps.hint: Think about what changes when a firm pushes output right up to this exact point rather than stopping earlier.

steps.q: Shareholders own the firm but do not run it day to day. When the managers running the firm achieve this maximum profit, what can be paid out to the owners from it?
steps.right: A larger payment to shareholders out of the profit
steps.wrong: A larger salary for the managers only
steps.hint: Profit belongs to the owners of the firm, not just the people managing it.
